transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

I came in because... well, I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I'll just lie awake in bed replaying client models in my head, and then I usually wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach completely tight. I end up going to work feeling like I never actually rested at all.
Are your worries mainly about work, or do they also involve several other parts of your life?

It's mostly work. I mean, I guess I worry about other things sometimes, like anyone else, but work is the main thing that keeps me up. It's just a constant loop in my head about the models and the projections. I don't really have those same intense worries about other parts of my life.
Did these sleep problems begin after a specific change or stressful event at work?

Yeah, it actually did. It's... well, this has been going on for about three years now. It started right after the merger that reorganized our Caribbean-market division. Ever since then, it's just been like this.
On nights when you are not worrying about work, do you still have trouble falling or staying asleep?

Honestly, I don't really know. There aren't many nights where I'm not worrying about work. It's pretty much a constant thing. So... I guess I haven't really noticed what my sleep is like without the work stress, because the stress is just always there.
If the work-related stress and worries suddenly went away, do you think you would still have trouble sleeping?

I'm really not sure. I mean, it's hard to even imagine the work stress just going away at this point. It's been there for so long. But... I suppose if it did, maybe I'd sleep better? I just don't know for certain since I haven't experienced a night without it in years.
How much does this worry interfere with your ability to function at work?

It interferes a lot. I mean, it's gotten to the point where I've actually received a formal performance warning. My financial models and my presentations just keep slipping, and I can't seem to stay on top of them anymore. 

And... it's not just at the office, really. I've completely stopped showing up for my volunteer teaching, my yoga classes, the book club I was in... all the things that used to keep my life outside of work intact. It's just taking a huge toll on everything.
Is the work-related situation that began these problems still ongoing?
Yeah, it is. Um... this has actually been going on for about three years now. It all started ever since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division. So, yes, it's definitely still ongoing.
When you lie awake at night, is your mind usually occupied by work worries, or do you also remain unable to sleep when your mind feels calm?

It's almost always the work worries. That's actually why I came in, to be honest, because I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I'll just lie awake replaying client models over and over in my head. And then... well, even if I do drift off, I usually wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning, and my stomach is just tight. I end up going to work feeling like I never actually rested. I don't really know what a calm mind feels like at night anymore.
Before the merger, did you have persistent difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep?
No, not really. I mean, before all of this started, I slept just fine. I might have had a restless night here and there, like anyone, but nothing like this. It really wasn't an issue back then.
